entries.title: Why staying hydrated matters
paragraphs: Water helps your body keep a normal temperature, lubricates and cushions your joints, and helps get rid of waste through urination, sweating, and bowel movements.
Not getting enough fluid can lead to dehydration.
You may need more fluid in hot weather, during physical activity, or when you are ill. Recommended daily water intake varies, for example by age, sex, and activity level.

This is general educational content reviewed by the project owner. It has not been clinically reviewed or clinically validated. For personal advice, consult a qualified healthcare professional. If you think you may be experiencing an emergency, contact local emergency services immediately.

evidence.section: Your body needs more water when you are
evidence.quote: In hot climates. More physically active. Running a fever. Having diarrhea or vomiting.

evidence.section: How to reduce the risk of dehydration
evidence.quote: Drink more when there's a higher risk of dehydrating. For example, if you're being sick, sweating due to hot weather or exercise, or you have diarrhoea.
